Ui.Script:
MIRRORTIMER_NUMTIMERS = 3
-- The bar colour per timer type, keyed by the name that arrives on the wire. DEATH is in -- the published set even though nothing in 1.12 ever raises a timer of that type - the -- table is the contract, so it carries the whole set and not just the three we see. MirrorTimerColors = { EXHAUSTION = { r = 1.00, g = 0.90, b = 0.00 }, BREATH = { r = 0.00, g = 0.50, b = 1.00 }, DEATH = { r = 1.00, g = 0.70, b = 0.00 }, FEIGNDEATH = { r = 1.00, g = 0.70, b = 0.00 }, }
-- Which bar `timer` belongs on. A bar already carrying it wins wherever it sits - the -- server re-sends a whole START on every change, and a re-STATE must land back in place -- instead of eating another bar; failing that the first idle bar takes it, and if all -- three are busy the timer simply goes unshown (see departure 2). local function claim_bar(timer) local idle for index = 1, MIRRORTIMER_NUMTIMERS do local bar = getglobal("MirrorTimer" .. index) if bar:IsVisible() then if bar.timer == timer then return bar end elseif not idle then idle = bar end end return idle end
-- Hand a bar back to the pool: off screen, holding nothing. local function release_bar(bar) bar:Hide() bar.timer = nil end
-- Raise or re-seat one timer. Milliseconds on the wire, seconds on the bar; `scale` is -- the server's signed rate, which OnUpdate integrates from here. function MirrorTimer_Show(timer, value, maxvalue, scale, paused, label) local bar = claim_bar(timer) if not bar then return nil end
bar.timer = timer bar.value = value / 1000 bar.scale = scale bar.paused = paused > 0 and 1 or nil
local name = bar:GetName() getglobal(name .. "Text"):SetText(label)
local fill = getglobal(name .. "StatusBar") local color = MirrorTimerColors[timer] fill:SetMinMaxValues(0, maxvalue / 1000) fill:SetValue(bar.value) fill:SetStatusBarColor(color.r, color.g, color.b)
bar:Show() return bar end
function MirrorTimerFrame_OnLoad() -- The two events that address a timer already running... this:RegisterEvent("MIRROR_TIMER_PAUSE") this:RegisterEvent("MIRROR_TIMER_STOP") -- ...and the one that ends whatever this bar was holding. this:RegisterEvent("PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD") this.timer = nil end
function MirrorTimerFrame_OnEvent() if event == "PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD" then -- A worldport ends every timer the old world was running; a stale breath bar must -- not survive the loading screen. release_bar(this) return end -- Everything below names one running timer. Anything else is another bar's business. if not this:IsShown() or arg1 ~= this.timer then return end if event == "MIRROR_TIMER_PAUSE" then -- The flag rides in arg2 (departure 3), and absent means running. this.paused = (arg2 and arg2 > 0) and 1 or nil elseif event == "MIRROR_TIMER_STOP" then release_bar(this) end end
-- The whole of the client-side motion: between packets the bar walks itself along the -- rate the server named. Nothing here decides anything - drowning is the server's call. function MirrorTimerFrame_OnUpdate(frame, elapsed) if not frame.paused then frame.value = frame.value + frame.scale * elapsed getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "StatusBar"):SetValue(frame.value) end end
-- The ref's UIParent_OnEvent MIRROR_TIMER_START arm, rehosted (see departure 1). function MirrorTimerDriver_OnLoad() this:RegisterEvent("MIRROR_TIMER_START") end
function MirrorTimerDriver_OnEvent() MirrorTimer_Show(arg1, arg2, arg3, arg4, arg5, arg6) end
